tour.overview:
Doha is at its best in the hour around sunset, when the heat drops, the light turns gold over the water and the towers of West Bay begin to glow. This private evening tour puts you on the bay at exactly that moment, aboard a dhow – the wooden sailing boat that carried Qatar's pearl divers and traders for centuries – and then takes you into Souq Waqif when the old market is at its liveliest.

The dhow leaves from the old harbour on the Corniche and cruises slowly across Doha Bay: past the Museum of Islamic Art on its island, along the skyline of West Bay and back as the lights come on. Tea, coffee and water are served on board while your guide explains how pearling shaped the town and how the city grew around the bay. Back on land, you walk into Souq Waqif, where the evening crowds fill the lanes of spice and perfume shops, musicians play in the squares and the restaurants light their grills. Your guide shows you the Falcon Souq and the best places to eat, and you can stay on for dinner before the driver takes you back to your hotel.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 3 hours 30 minutes (late afternoon to evening)
• Start and finish: your hotel in Doha
• Type: private tour with car, driver, local guide and a private dhow (shared dhow on request for lower prices)
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Activity level: very easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Doha Bay and the old dhow harbour.
• The Museum of Islamic Art and MIA Park from the water.
• The West Bay skyline at sunset and after dark.
• Souq Waqif, the Falcon Souq and the evening squares.

WHY THIS TOUR WORKS
Doha's skyline is best seen from the water, and the souq is best in the evening. Combining the two in one private outing means no waiting for a group boat, a cruise timed for the sunset and a guide who knows where locals actually eat.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Couples, families, stopover travellers with an evening in Doha, photographers, and anyone who wants a relaxed first or last night in Qatar.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For museums and the city by day, choose our Doha private city tour. For dunes and adventure, the desert safari to the Inland Sea.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Wear comfortable shoes and modest clothes for the souq. A light layer helps on the water from November to March. Dinner is not included; Souq Waqif has restaurants for every budget.

days.name: Evening Dhow Cruise & Souq Waqif
days.description:
What to expect: a private sunset cruise on a traditional dhow across Doha Bay, then Souq Waqif after dark with a local guide.

Your guide and driver collect you from your hotel in the late afternoon and drive along the Corniche to the old dhow harbour, where the wooden boats are moored below the skyline. The dhow is the classic boat of the Gulf: for centuries these hand-built hulls took Qatar's pearl divers out to the oyster banks each summer and carried dates, cloth and spices between the Gulf ports. Today they are painted, carpeted and lit with strings of lights for evening cruises.

On board you are served tea, Arabic coffee and water as the dhow slips out into Doha Bay. The route passes close to the Museum of Islamic Art, I. M. Pei's limestone building standing on its own island, then follows the West Bay skyline – the torch-shaped and cylindrical towers that went up in the 2000s and 2010s – as the sun sets and the buildings light up. Your guide tells you how the bay once filled with pearling boats and how the city grew from a fishing village into a capital in two generations.

Back on shore, a short drive brings you to Souq Waqif just as it comes alive. In the evening the lanes fill with families and visitors, the spice and perfume shops stay open late, musicians and artisans gather in the squares and the restaurants light their charcoal grills. Your guide walks you through the main lanes to the Falcon Souq, where trained falcons sit on perches waiting for buyers, and points out the best places for Qatari, Lebanese or Persian food. Stay for dinner (not included), and when you are ready the driver takes you back to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates; adjusted to the sunset)
16:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
16:30 – Dhow harbour on the Corniche; boarding.
16:45 – Dhow cruise on Doha Bay at sunset (about 1 hour).
18:00 – Souq Waqif after dark and the Falcon Souq (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
19:30 – Dinner in the souq (optional, not included) or return to your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Sunset is around 16:45 in December and around 18:20 in June; we set the start time when we confirm your request.
• The dhow is stable and the bay is calm, so seasickness is rare.
• A shared dhow is cheaper; ask us if you prefer it.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, English-speaking local guide, private dhow cruise, tea, coffee and water on board, hotel pick-up.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose your date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only once your tour is confirmed.

faq.question: What time does the tour start?
faq.answer: About an hour and a quarter before sunset, so you are on the water for the golden hour: around 15:30 in December and around 17:00 in summer. We confirm the exact time with your request.

faq.question: Is the dhow private?
faq.answer: Yes, the standard tour uses a private dhow for your group. A shared dhow is available on request at a lower price.

faq.question: Is food served on the boat?
faq.answer: Tea, Arabic coffee and water are included. Dinner is not; most travellers eat in Souq Waqif after the cruise, where there are restaurants for every budget.

faq.question: Can children join?
faq.answer: Yes. The dhow has railings and seating, and children wear life jackets on board. Child seats in the car are available on request.

faq.question: Will I get seasick?
faq.answer: Very unlikely. Doha Bay is sheltered and calm, and the dhow moves slowly.

faq.question: Can I do this tour on a layover?
faq.answer: Yes, if you have an evening between flights and can enter Qatar. We can pick you up at Hamad International Airport and bring you back in time.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and clothes covering shoulders and knees for the souq. Bring a light jacket on the water from November to March.

faq.question: Is alcohol served?
faq.answer: No. Alcohol is not served on dhows or in Souq Waqif; it is available only in licensed hotels.

faq.question: Can we buy falcons or spices in the souq?
faq.answer: You can buy spices, perfumes, sweets and crafts. Falcons are sold, but exporting one requires permits; most visitors just watch.

faq.question: Can we combine this with the city tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Many travellers do the Doha city tour in the morning and this cruise in the evening; we can plan both on the same day.

faq.question: When is the best time of year?
faq.answer: October to April, when evenings are pleasant. In summer evenings are hot and humid but the breeze on the water helps.

faq.question: What is your cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Before your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
